newsitem.title: GERMANY: Luxembourg's Juncker criticises German euro debate.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg's Juncker criticises German euro debate.

text.p: Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker criticised on Tuesday a debate in Germany over how strictly the entry criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU) should be interpreted.

Juncker told Germany's MDR radio the discussion underscoring a growing rift between Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) and Bavarian sister party, Christian Social Union (CSU), was damaging for the project.
He was speaking on the day his country took over the rotating European Union presidency.
"I find this German discussion unhealthy," Juncker said.

Kohl's conservative CSU coalition partners say EU states wanting to join the launch of Europe's planned single currency, the euro, must limit budget deficits to precisely 3.0 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) as a guarantee of stability.

The CSU's position has been personified by the powerful Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber who commentators say is heading for a collision with Kohl, whose more moderate CDU argues three percent could be interpreted as 3.1 or more.

"The fact is that in the (Maastricht) treaty there is only one figure. That is three percent. And the treaty also states under which circumstances a global political judgement can be made as to when this must not be 3.0 precisely," he said.
Juncker warned Germans that those who speak of softening the criteria were giving the wrong signal to other EU capitals.

"In other countries many people are now saying that, judging by (German) public opinion, Germans are partly willing to accept a softening of the criteria," he said. "That would suggest we do not need to make an effort anymore."
Juncker also dismissed a report in German news magazine, Der Spiegel, which he said gave the impression he had said he did not rule out a delay in the timetable for EMU.
"I am strictly and absolutely opposed to a delay in the (planned 1999) EMU launch," Juncker said.
